links_touching_record.rationale: FB2-SW-SIR-000004 is the software interface requirement set for the platform service and serial bus boundary and is specified by FB2-SW-IFS-000007 (OS and platform abstraction) and FB2-SW-IFS-000008 (SPI, I2C and UART drivers). The direction is specification to requirement, which is the direction a requirement is written in: the interface specification establishes what the interface is by analysing the source at the pinned commit, and the requirement states what must be true of it. This is the opposite of the direction the three existing FB2-SW-SWR-* requirements were produced in - those are back-inferred from the implementation and their revision history says so - and naming the relationship explicitly is what keeps the two directions distinguishable. Every statement in the requirement is traceable to a named element of the specification, and the requirement carries that traceability as a field rather than leaving it in prose.

The second specification FB2-SW-SIR-000004 is derived from. FB2-SW-SIR-000004 covers the platform service and serial bus boundary and its derivation field names every interface specification it came from; this link names the second one so that a reader following the requirement to its evidence reaches both specifications rather than only the first. The direction and the reason are the same as for the first specification: the specification establishes what the interface is by analysing the source, and the requirement states what must be true of it.

The triage record classifies five of its seven dispositions against the platform-service interface-requirement record, including the one it classifies as mis-derived and the one it classifies as partially satisfied. The record carries a deliberate correction to that requirement's basis text for one element, and the correction is recorded in the triage rather than applied to the requirement; this link declares the dependency that correction rests on.

asil_justification.statement: Not applicable, and deliberately so. This requirement carries no safety allocation because the item it describes has not been through a hazard analysis and risk assessment, so there is no severity or exposure rating to derive an ASIL from. No ASIL is asserted for the real product and none is asserted here. This is not a statement that the interface is unimportant: it is a statement that the classification apparatus is not available in this repository, and a reader must not read 'not_applicable' as 'no consequence'.

authority_and_independence.independence_statement: Authored by an AI agent. It is a derivation from an analysed specification, not an elicitation, not an analysis of a higher-level requirement, and not independent review.

derivation.authoring_independence_statement: Authored by an AI agent from the interface specifications and the source. No requirements engineer confirmed that this is the interface that was wanted, no stakeholder stated a need that these requirements answer, and no human approved them. They record what the code obliges a consumer to rely on; they do not record what anyone asked for.
derivation.method: Every statement below names the interface element it obliges and the analysed behaviour it rests on.

element_requirements.basis: Neither element contains a depth counter, so a nested entry followed by a single exit leaves the masking in place. The two elements also mask different things - scheduling for the calling task versus interrupts globally - and the headers do not say so.
element_requirements.statement: A masking entry point shall state what it excludes and shall reject a nested entry.

element_requirements.basis: NOT satisfied by the analysed implementation. The element returns a tick count and the conversion constant is a separate macro elsewhere in the same layer.
element_requirements.statement: The time base shall state its unit and its resolution at the interface.

element_requirements.basis: NOT satisfied by the analysed implementation. When the bus is busy the entire body is skipped and the caller receives the success value.
element_requirements.statement: A serial read shall report a transfer that did not start as a failure.

element_requirements.basis: The claim returns a bare negative with no timing information and the release writes the idle state with no test of the previous state, so a lost release is indistinguishable from a correct one.
element_requirements.statement: A lock shall state its owner, its timeout and the consequence of a release that the caller does not hold.

element_requirements.basis: NOT satisfied by the analysed implementation. The I2C read asserts only that the length is greater than zero, and the UART read records the absence of a check as a deliberate suppression. Neither bounds the length against the buffer.
element_requirements.statement: Every transfer-length parameter shall be bounded against the destination buffer the caller supplies.

record_verbatim.element_requirements_note: The failure reaction of this boundary is almost entirely absent, which is why five of five requirements are unsatisfied. A skipped transfer looks like a completed one, a lock release cannot be refused, a masked section cannot be detected as nested, and two buffer lengths are unbounded. In every case the consumer has no channel through which to learn that something did not happen. That is recorded here as a property of the boundary rather than as a verdict on the code, and it is the reason this requirement set exists at all.
record_verbatim.failure_reaction: Five of five are unsatisfied by the implementation as analysed, and this record does not claim otherwise. That ratio is the finding, not a defect in this record. This is the boundary where the analysed code's own decisions are recorded as deliberate - the unchecked identifier, the unchecked lengths, the non-nesting masking - and the requirements state what the interface would have to do for a consumer to rely on it. Three of the five are one-line changes in intent: a range check, a unit in a comment, and a check on the skipped path. The other two, the lock ownership and the nesting, need a design decision.
not_established_by_this_record: Every requirement in this set is unsatisfied by the implementation as analysed. The record exists to state what the interface would owe a consumer, and it must not be read as a description of what the code does today.

Requirement A covers two elements that mask different things, and the requirement does not choose between them. Whether the global interrupt mask should detect nesting at all is a design decision for a hardware engineer, not something this record decides.
No requirement here is elicited from a stakeholder, a system requirement or a safety goal.
The requirement set states no bus speed, bit rate or protocol version for any of the three serial buses, because none appears in any of the three headers.
No ASIL, no safety allocation, no conformity claim, no certification, no human approval.
No verification has been performed against any of these requirements and no test measure exists for any of them.
record_verbatim.rationale: These requirements exist because the analysed boundaries fail in ways a consumer cannot detect from the outside. The I2C read reports a skipped transfer as success when the bus is busy, so a caller can believe it holds data it does not have. The SPI lock has no owner, no timeout and no refusal on a spurious release, so a lost release is indistinguishable from a correct one and a refused claim carries no timing information. Two buffer-length parameters are explicitly unchecked by a decision recorded in the source. A masking entry point that cannot detect nesting is the third such case. None of these is visible in a signature, and all four are the kind of property an interface requirement exists to state.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: Five interface requirements over the platform-service and serial-bus boundaries, derived from FB2-SW-IFS-000007 and FB2-SW-IFS-000008. Two of them are stated because the analysed interfaces do not satisfy them, and both concern failure detection: a transfer that never started is reported as a success, and a lock release is not checked.

safety_allocation.mitigation: No ASIL is allocated to this requirement. It is a software interface requirement about how two modules call each other, and the product it describes has never had a hazard analysis and risk assessment: no ISO 26262 conformity, no ASIL determination and no certification is claimed for it or for anything in this corpus. The non-applicability is stated with its reason rather than left blank, because an unexplained non-applicability is indistinguishable from a requirement that quietly dropped out of every ASIL-derived view.

standards_mappings.rationale: Supplies software interface requirements, the family SWE.1 expected and that was absent. It does not analyse them from a higher-level requirement, so the process's defining activity is still absent.

Backs SWE.1 with the software interface requirement family. The status stays partially_mapped because these requirements are derived from an analysis of an existing implementation, not analysed from software requirements or system requirements, and because the existing software requirements remain back-inferred.

Consumes the interface specifications this requirement set is derived from. A requirement derived from a specification is the direction that makes the specification the engineering content and this the obligation.

record_verbatim.statement: The platform-service and serial-bus interfaces shall present the following to their consumers: (a) a masking entry point that states what it excludes and that rejects a nested entry; (b) a time base that states its unit and its resolution; (c) a serial read that reports a transfer which did not start as a failure rather than a success; (d) a lock that states its owner, its timeout and the consequence of a release that the caller does not hold; and (e) a transfer length parameter that is bounded against the destination buffer the caller supplies.
record_verbatim.title: Software interface requirements: the platform-service and serial-bus interfaces

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-SW-SIR-000004` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. NEVER record the approval in revision_history - doing so stales every link pinning this revision and invalidates every stored review digest. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
